      "partial_result": "# Review of the In-Shop nonlinear-head proposal (HEAD b524a10b)\n\n**Verdict: conditional approval, with five required corrections. Two of them (C1 and C2) are blocking.** As written, the test gives an uninterpretable null and licenses a follow-up screen at the wrong training horizon. With the corrections it works as a cheap one-sided kill filter, which is the only thing it can honestly be.\n\nI edited nothing and launched nothing. The protected `topk.rs` still hashes to `1ae7f50a\u2026c0cb587`.\n\n## Fable's STOP: where I agree and where it overreaches\n\n- **The \"every composition\" claim is wrong as stated.** The SigLIP pooler outputs `h + MLP(LN(h))`. A residual added after the pooler, `U\u00b7gelu(D\u00b7z)`, adds depth after that sum, so the trained recipe does not strictly contain it. In practice the two are close. The real difference is where the nonlinearity sits and its learning rate: head LR 1e-4 versus the pooler at vision LR 1e-5. Your reframing as \"activation placement\" is correct.\n- **Fable's asymmetry runs the wrong way.** It said a pass can't license anything and a fail only adds a ledger entry. The cached control has no trainable nonlinearity at all, while the deployed recipe trains the pooler MLP. So a cached **pass** is expected whether or not placement matters, and it tells us little. A cached **fail** is the informative outcome: if curvature doesn't help even when it is the only trainable nonlinearity, it is unlikely to help on top of a trained pooler. The test is therefore action-bearing only as a kill filter in front of a GPU run. At about 180 s of CPU that is still worth doing.\n- **Is it distinct from the closed arms?** Yes, from width, head warm-up and the rank-16 token adapter: those test a different channel or a training phase. It is **not** a new idea, though. The scope should list three negatives from the same family:\n  - The Cars zero-init rank-32 GELU residual (`similarity_negative_results_2026-09-19.md:287`). Its control was affine-only, so parameter counts did not match.\n  - The ReLU residual in `JointRelationalEncoder`, which failed its incremental gate (`docs/relational_linear_compaction.md:93`). The scope asked for this to be inspected, and the proposal does not cite it.\n  - The SigLIP2-base 1.31M-parameter nonlinear correction: +1.23 mAP@R, +0.10 R@1, one seed negative. This predicts a \"mAP moves, R@1 doesn't\" pattern, and the conjunctive gate correctly kills that.\n\n## Required corrections\n\n**C1. The GELU is almost linear at initialization (checked in the code). Blocking.**\n- `initialize_head_and_classifier` and `probe_inshop_head_warmup.py:30` feed the head `F.normalize(source)`, so the input has unit norm.\n- The existing residual uses `kaiming_uniform_(a=\u221a5)` on fan-in 1024. That gives weight std \u2248 0.018, so the pre-activation std is \u2248 0.018.\n- In that range GELU(z) \u2248 0.5z + 0.4z\u00b2. The quadratic term is about 1.4% of the linear one.\n- So the treatment starts as a half-gain *linear* residual. Against an identity control, that is an effective-learning-rate confound, not a curvature contrast.\n- The same init applied in the Cars run, which weakens that closure too. It still shouldn't be reopened.\n- Fix:\n  - Rescale the shared `D` so the pre-activation std on inner-train rows is 1. This is one label-free scalar, frozen and hashed, and identical in both arms.\n  - Make the control activation `0.5\u00b7z` (GELU's slope at zero) instead of identity, so both arms get the same first-order gradient on `U`.\n  - Record, frozen in advance, the fraction of the final treatment residual's energy on inner-val rows that its best linear fit does not explain. A null counts as a closure only if that fraction is \u2265 0.10. Below that, record \"degenerate, uninformative\" and still stop, with no retuning.\n\n**C2. The follow-up is set at the wrong training horizon. Blocking.**\n- The repo's own direct256 evidence shows a head-side capacity advantage of +0.80 pp R@1 at 100 updates shrinking to +0.24 pp at 1000.\n- A 100-update screen is the horizon most inflated by transient head capacity, and a nonlinear head at 10\u00d7 the encoder LR is exactly that kind of capacity. A pass at 100 updates therefore can't bear on the deployed 1000-update recipe.\n- Fix: a pass may only license proposing one paired 1000-update image-level test. Use the `freeze_emb`, seed 179024 recipe with the encoder settings unchanged.
